title: Antibiotics Gradient Assay for V. natriegens
author: Franziska Müller
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ps8dnhw
materials: Diltute the preculture to an OD550 of 0.1.

steps.title: Prepare overnight preculture
steps.instruction: Inoculate Vibrio natriegens into LB3 medium (3 % NaCl) and incubate with shaking overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Create first agar layer with antibiotics
steps.instruction: Place 11.5 × 11.5 cm plates in an inclined position so that the agar thickness tapers to zero at one edge, then pour 30 mL of LB3 agar containing the chosen antibiotic concentrations to be tested into each plate and allow the agar to solidify.

steps.title: Add second antibiotic‑free agar layer
steps.instruction: Turn each plate onto a flat, even surface and carefully pour an additional 30 mL of LB3 agar without any antibiotics on top of the first solidified layer; let this second layer solidify completely.

steps.title: Spot inoculate culture along gradient
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, place 8–10 spots of 5 µL of the overnight V. natriegens culture onto the surface of the solidified agar, arranging the spots along the antibiotic gradient.

steps.title: Dry and incubate plates
steps.instruction: Allow the inoculated spots to air‑dry, then incubate the plates upside‑down either at 37 °C overnight or at room temperature over the weekend.

steps.title: Measure growth boundary
steps.instruction: After incubation, measure the distance from the nearest edge of the agar plate to the furthest point of visible bacterial growth for each spot.

steps.title: Calculate highest survivable concentration
steps.instruction: Compute the highest antibiotic concentration V. natriegens can survive (c_antibioticH) using the equation: c_antibioticH = c_antibioticmax × d_growth / d_plate, where c_antibioticmax is the concentration used in the lower (first) agar layer, d_growth is the measured distance from the plate edge to the last growth point, and d_plate is the plate length (11.5 cm).
